Answers running, exited, abandoned, gate-incomplete, or unknown — never a
partial answer. A job whose supervisor is gone without an outcome reads as
unknown rather than as success, which is what makes it safe to act on:
unknown, abandoned, and gate-incomplete are exactly as terminal as exited,
never a reason to keep waiting and never a success whatever the raw exit
code says. gate-incomplete means this job's own process ended while a job
it started had not reached a verdict; abandoned means it left other work it
started running in its own process group, unsupervised. A job's own
process exiting is therefore never the verdict on its own -- this job's own
eventual state is, including for a nested job it started after that process
already exited: it waits for that job before reporting exited, folding a
failure into startedJobFailed rather than letting its own clean exit code
hide it. Finished jobs stay readable for 24 hours so a caller that
reconnects after the work ended can still learn what happened.

aliveAgeMs is the milliseconds since the supervisor's last ~1s beat,
computed in erun's own clock so nothing subtracts a pod timestamp from a
caller's clock. Once it exceeds 5000, treat the job as failed (an unknown
outcome, never a success, never a tool error) even if state has not caught
up yet; a silent-but-healthy command never trips this, since the beat does
not depend on the work's own output.

Usage:
  erun job status [flags]

Examples:
  erun exec job status --tenant team --environment dev
  erun exec job status --tenant team --environment dev --id suite --output json

Flags:
      --dry-run              Resolve and trace mutating actions without executing them.
      --environment string   Environment the job runs in
  -h, --help                 help for status
      --id string            Job to report; omit for every retained job
      --tenant string        Tenant whose environment the job belongs to

Global Flags:
      --output string   Result format: text (default, human stream) or json (structured result on stdout for orchestrators). (default "text")
      --time            Print the elapsed runtime after the command finishes.
  -v, --verbose count   Increase verbosity: -v streams external tool output, -vv adds erun command traces.
